Build your own visual world

Integrate, regenerate and synthesise

Produce a systematic body of work that integrates conventions and regenerates ideas within painting practice

Suggested teaching time
18–22 weeks

Timing, task steps and quantities are classroom suggestions, not NZQA grade requirements.

Read the standard (PDF)

The brief

How can my painting inquiry become a coherent, personal visual world?

Develop an independent painting inquiry grounded in a personally meaningful proposition. Bring conventions together, return to your own ideas and reform them through new work. Curate a systematic body in which the progression, integration and regeneration are visible across the whole inquiry.

Materials & preparation

Your own research and visual sources, selected painting media and supports, a working diary, and three hinged portfolio panels for the physical painting route.

Use your own drawings and photographs as starting points. Record sources and seek permission for people, places and culturally significant material. Discuss tikanga and context with your teacher where relevant.

This is an external standard. Use the activities as teaching suggestions; make your own decisions during assessed work. Your teacher must keep support within NZQA’s annual conditions.

Artist connections

Choose the connections that serve your intention. The contemporary models offer different approaches; select a relevant comparison rather than studying every artist. These works are references, not assessment exemplars.

Compare how a painting language brings material decisions together with a sustained position or question. Integrate selected conventions and regenerate ideas within your own culturally situated inquiry.

  • Emily Karaka

    Contemporary Māori · Aotearoa New Zealand

    Karaka’s energetic colour, gesture and text connect painting with whenua, whānau and Māori sovereignty. Investigate how the marks carry a political and personal position; read that position alongside the painted surface.

    Sharjah Art Foundation · Ka Awatea, A New Dawn · Painting investigation

  • Shane Cotton

    Contemporary Māori · Aotearoa New Zealand

    Cotton reworks historical references to investigate bicultural identity and colonisation. Compare how recurring forms change meaning through placement, scale and surrounding space, while keeping their particular cultural histories in view.

    Gow Langsford · artist profile and paintings · Painting investigation

  • Julie Mehretu

    Contemporary · Ethiopia / United States

    Mehretu’s layered abstractions bring drawing and painting into dialogue with place, history and movement. Follow how overlapping marks and structures can make several spatial readings coexist.

    Whitney Museum · survey, paintings and resources · Painting investigation

  • Mark Bradford

    Contemporary · United States

    Bradford’s building-up and removal of paper connects material process with the social life of a city. Read his account of collage and décollage, then ask how adding and removing can each generate an idea.

    Art21 · artist interview on process and materials · Painting investigation

  • Frances Hodgkins

    Aotearoa New Zealand / Britain

    Look at how still-life objects and landscape can share a painted space. Try shifting the relationship between an object, its surroundings and its colour.

    Christchurch Art Gallery · Still Life

Artwork reproduction rights and assessment permission are different. A reusable image on this site is not automatically suitable for your assessed portfolio. Read the external conditions.

Studio sequence

Use this as a flexible route through the learning. Let the work suggest the next move.

  1. Frame an independent inquiry

    Develop a proposition with enough scope for sustained investigation. Gather and generate original imagery, examine relevant artist practices and identify pictorial relationships you want to investigate.

  2. Bring conventions together

    Make initial works that combine selected methods toward your intention. Test how the conventions interact; avoid simply placing one artist’s manner beside another’s. Select a promising relationship for further work.

  3. Develop and regenerate

    Evaluate the work, return to an earlier productive idea and re-form it in new paintings. Repeat the cycle as the inquiry develops. Regeneration must be evident in the body, not reserved for an optional final experiment.

  4. Deepen the relationships

    Critically compare the conceptual and technical decisions. Refine the relationship between sources, methods and intentions, and explore further options. Seek an integrated personal language rather than a sequence of borrowed appearances.

  5. Curate the whole body

    Select and order the work so the inquiry can be followed across the portfolio. Look for gaps, redundant repetition and unsupported changes. Resolve the presentation, complete authenticity documentation and follow the current external specifications.

A useful studio conversation

Put two related works side by side. Describe what changed, show the evidence and explain what you will investigate next. Invite feedback, then make your own decision.

Presentation & submission

For the 2026 physical painting route, submit three hinged portrait panels, each 820 × 610 mm; the folded portfolio must be within 1 kg and 15 mm. All paint must be dry. The alternative actual time-based moving-image route is one video up to 180 seconds, with an authenticity statement. A filmed slideshow of boards is not that alternative.

Read the full 2026 NZQA specifications (PDF) and external assessment conditions. These are year-specific requirements; confirm any updates for your assessment year.

What changes between grades?

Student-friendly guidance adapted from the standard. The whole body of relevant evidence determines the grade; the examples below illustrate possibilities.

Grade distinctions for AS91456
GradeWhat the evidence needs to show
AchievementCombine conventions and regenerate ideas within an ordered, related body.In this task: The body visibly brings methods together and reforms earlier ideas in new work.
MeritIntegrate particular conventions purposefully and regenerate selected ideas toward an intention.In this task: Considered combinations and returns contribute clearly to the intended outcomes.
ExcellenceSynthesise critically selected ideas and methods, regenerating a depth of ideas.In this task: Sources, conventions and personal intentions work as an integrated language that opens further possibilities.

Authority: NZQA AS91456 achievement criteria and explanatory notes (PDF).

Watch for

Three panels of technically accomplished paintings can still lack integrated conventions or regenerated ideas.

Pause & reflect

Where do conventions become your own language? Identify a passage in the body where several sources or methods have become inseparable from your intention.

These optional working notes belong to you. This website does not submit assessment evidence.

Teacher notes

Planning, assessment & differentiation

Check regeneration at Achievement as well as at higher grades. Assess the body holistically using the current schedule and exemplars; separate strong technique from the depth and integration of ideas. The 2026 physical painting route is a three-panel portfolio. Keep work student-led and assistance within the annual conditions.

Support and stretch

For teaching practice, reduce the number of simultaneous choices, model one material process and invite oral discussion alongside drawing. Offer vocabulary prompts and accessible media. To extend the learning, ask students to compare alternatives, justify a rejection or investigate a consequence of their own decision. Adapt assessed support to the standard’s conditions and any approved arrangements.

Before issuing the task

Set local start and finish dates, agree available materials and check the current standard, conditions and exemplars. Use school authenticity processes and your normal moderation procedures. Adjust this brief to the class and context; it has not been quality assured by NZQA.
